name: The Collection
about: Everything Grant has built, running inside Aviary with no internet. Each exhibit is a copy; the originals stay exactly where they are.

enclosures.name: The Wally House
enclosures.blurb: Every Wally2TTD there has ever been — two generations of the tower defense, the Godot port, the spin-offs, and the tools that keep track of them all.

enclosures.name: The Jurassic Paddock
enclosures.blurb: Jurassic Empire, the dinosaur park sim — playable right here — with its website, its roadmap and the timeline that started it.

enclosures.name: The Arcade
enclosures.blurb: Games that aren't Wally or Jurassic: a light-for-health survivor, the first chapter of a desktop mystery, and the site for a sci-fi game stranded across dimensions.

enclosures.name: The Reading Room
enclosures.blurb: Deep-dive pages: consoles twice over, PC specs, gaming brands, the cost of A.I., a ratings archive, a work log and a dev log.

enclosures.name: The Workshop
enclosures.blurb: Tools and apps — a chat app, a video-tool concept, a pocket calculator in C, an office suite in a page, a battery that charges itself, and Aviary's own pages.

enclosures.name: Keepsakes
enclosures.blurb: Two pages made for a birthday.

shelves.gen1: Generation 1 · the originals and their remasters
shelves.archive: The archive · backups and alternate cuts

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v1.9 Director's Cut
exhibits.blurb: The live v1.9 and the one to play, full stop. No keypad, waves that end when the last zombie does, speed control, synthesised sound and a rebalance that gives all four towers a job.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v1.8 Remastered
exhibits.blurb: v1.8's engine and palette carrying everything Gen 2 ever built: thirteen turrets, twelve enemies, wave Directives, the Warden medic — and a switch that fades back to the 2025 look mid-wave.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD 2.4.2
exhibits.short: The Godot port · now in the browser
exhibits.blurb: The command-deck tower defense rebuilt in a real engine, with sound. Exported for the web so it plays here — the desktop build is Wally2TTD-2.4.2.exe.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD 2.4.1 & 2.4.2
exhibits.blurb: The experimental 2.4.1 and the Godot 2.4.2 side by side: what changed, what didn't, and a Play button for each — both run here.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v2 PROTO
exhibits.note: Commander Bart, its AI advisor, never answers — the build was saved with an empty API key, as it always was.
exhibits.blurb: The Gen-2 restart in 33 KB: four turrets, three zombie types, no wave cap, and Commander Bart asking an AI for five-word orders.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v2.1
exhibits.blurb: The prototype rewritten properly: a real CONFIG, a hard 100-wave cap and the Walker / Runner / Brute names. The first version that feels balanced.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v2.2
exhibits.blurb: The arsenal doubles to eight — Arc, Mortar, and the Amp and Cryo support auras — and Tier 3 upgrades become a choice rather than a bigger number.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v2.3
exhibits.blurb: Scout, Guard and Breacher join the enemy side, and a five-panel command rail reads the field live. The most informative build to learn on.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v2.4.1 EXP
exhibits.blurb: The branch that gave the series its first boss: every tenth wave a TITAN with 1800 HP, armour and half-strength Cryo. The build 2.4.2 was ported from.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v2.4
exhibits.blurb: The widest classic roster: Gatling and Lancer, Raider and Bulwark, and a System Insight advisor naming what's clustering. The richest Gen-2 build to play.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v1.8
exhibits.blurb: Where the perimeter starts: a Pistol Cannon, a Sniper Beam and a Mini-Gun Array against three zombie families on one L-shaped road.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v1.9 Director's Cut (Old)
exhibits.note: Kept for the archive, not for playing — it still asks for its PIN. Play the current cut instead.
exhibits.blurb: A Gen-1 remaster built after the whole v2 line: third tiers, a Scout, and Golden Waves every tenth round — behind a keypad.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD v1.8 · desktop edition
exhibits.short: The page inside the Electron app
exhibits.blurb: v1.8 as it shipped inside the "Wally2TTD Strategic Defense" desktop wrapper — two bytes away from the original.

exhibits.title: Tidepool Siege
exhibits.blurb: The formula goes underwater: coral pods hold a trench for 100 strata, and it ends on a 24,000-HP Abyss King.

exhibits.title: Silver v1.4
exhibits.blurb: An idle mining game at the outpost before the invasion. Dig through five strata while the radio counts down and the sky above you reddens — then it hands off to Wally2TTD.

exhibits.title: Silver v1.3
exhibits.blurb: The fourth alpha of the prequel — every one traded something away; v1.4 was the rewrite that kept it all.

exhibits.title: Silver v1.2
exhibits.blurb: The third alpha of the mining prequel.

exhibits.title: Silver v1.1
exhibits.short: A quiet outpost in the hills · 銀
exhibits.blurb: The second alpha — the one that put 銀, silver, in the title.

exhibits.title: Silver v1.0
exhibits.short: Sector mining outpost · before the wall
exhibits.blurb: The very first Silver: a mining outpost before the perimeter, before the wall.

exhibits.title: Wally2TTD Radio
exhibits.blurb: A radio receiver with three public stations, a live signal meter — and a classified fourth channel past the end of the band. Every sound is generated live.

exhibits.title: The Full Evolution
exhibits.short: Five versions, Gemini v1.8 to Codex v2.3
exhibits.note: Made as a chat widget, so outside that chat its colours come out plain.
exhibits.blurb: An early side-by-side history of the series — which AI built which version, and what each one added.

exhibits.title: The Wally2TTD Hub
exhibits.short: The front door to the series
exhibits.blurb: Every build with its rosters, a compare deck and the tooling — the one surface where the whole series is visible at once.

exhibits.title: The Version Atlas
exhibits.blurb: The series' timeline of record: every build expanded with its real mechanics and leftover comments, a size-growth curve and a lore codex. Also ships as its own .exe.

exhibits.title: The Wally2TTD Launcher
exhibits.short: Desktop command deck · v0.9.1 Track Sync
exhibits.note: A Windows program, so it can't run inside a browser — this is its landing page.
exhibits.blurb: Finds every build in its folder, watches for new ones, tracks playtime per build and crowns your most-played. Built with the C# compiler that ships with Windows.

exhibits.title: WallyCore1
exhibits.note: An engine add-on for Godot projects, not a game — this is its landing page.
exhibits.blurb: The engine layer under the Wally and Jurassic games: synthesised audio and music, saves, scene flow, a debug overlay, two renderers — and a self-test that must pass 120 of 120.

exhibits.title: v1.9 Director's Cut · Unlocked
exhibits.blurb: Saved fifteen minutes after the Director's Cut, with the keypad gone and nothing else changed.

exhibits.title: v1.9 DC · Unlocked 2 (backup, 27 Aug)
exhibits.blurb: A safety copy taken before the Director's Cut was repaired into the current cut.

exhibits.title: v1.9 DC · Unlocked 2 (pre-v1.9.2, 29 Aug)
exhibits.blurb: Saved on 29 August, just before the changes that made it the current cut.

exhibits.title: v2.4 · Rail Ops Crisis
exhibits.blurb: A v2.4 rebuilt around milestone incidents and boss-wave dispatches — one of the two cuts before the flagship.

exhibits.title: v2.4 · Compact Command Deck
exhibits.blurb: Twenty-three minutes later: offline directive drafting, tighter tactical panels and a stability pass.

exhibits.title: Jurassic Empire
exhibits.blurb: Build the park, balance the divisions, keep the fences powered. The game's own web export — it plays right here; the desktop build is JurassicEmpire.exe.

exhibits.title: Jurassic Empire · the website
exhibits.note: Its download button points at the 105 MB JurassicEmpire.exe, which stays in its own folder.
exhibits.blurb: The game's marketing site — four islands, 43 species, and dinosaurs drawn by the game's own renderer, ported to the page.

exhibits.title: The Dig Plan
exhibits.short: The series roadmap as an excavation
exhibits.blurb: 2026 to 2028 drawn as a dig site: depth is time, and the deeper the band, the less certain the plan.

exhibits.title: Jurassic Chronicles
exhibits.note: Its styling is fetched from the internet (Tailwind) — offline it shows as plain text.
exhibits.blurb: Thirty-two years and seven feature films, from 65 million BC to 2025, laid out as a dossier.

exhibits.title: EMBER
exhibits.blurb: A dark-arena survivor where your light is your health, your vision and your timer — one number doing three jobs.

exhibits.title: THE LOST · Part 1
exhibits.blurb: A narrative mystery told through a desktop that boots itself: a POST screen, a main menu, settings and a changelog — and something wrong underneath.

exhibits.title: PARALLAX
exhibits.note: The game's site, not the game — John Morgan, the Xenars and Megatonic are still being built. "Join the Quantum Division" now really sends your email (needs internet); the original page is kept untouched as history.
exhibits.blurb: The site for Grant's hard sci-fi survival game: stranded across dimensions on an alien-occupied Earth, where every message home arrives 72 seconds late.

exhibits.title: The Console Index
exhibits.blurb: PS4 to ROG Xbox Ally X compared on price, performance, hardware and how much of each the OS eats.

exhibits.title: Spec Showdown
exhibits.blurb: Grant's GTC-120 — a 9800X3D and an RTX 5070 Ti — against three other machines, spec by spec.

exhibits.title: The Complete ROG Experience
exhibits.blurb: A brand dossier: laptops, handhelds, monitors, components and the ecosystem that ties them together.

exhibits.title: The A.I. Ledger
exhibits.blurb: The A.I. economy in 2026: who owns the market, what subscriptions and tokens cost, and the electricity bill nobody signed for.

exhibits.title: The Game Ledger
exhibits.blurb: Every game played, rated and remembered.

exhibits.title: Work Log №01
exhibits.blurb: Two weeks of game-dev: Jurassic Empire, WallyCore1, Wally2TTD, a new 3D project — and the priority order that finally got written down.

exhibits.title: Dev Log
exhibits.short: The projects, in the order they happened
exhibits.blurb: A development portfolio: Jurassic Empire, WallyCore1, Wally2TTD and a first 3D project, each with where it stands — and NewsBits and the other work around them.

exhibits.title: Console Spectrum
exhibits.blurb: An interactive atlas of PlayStation, Xbox and the ROG Xbox Ally X, made the same day as the Console Index — and arguing that the more powerful machine is never the whole answer.

exhibits.title: Artemis
exhibits.short: A chat app on your own AI
exhibits.note: Chats with your own AI right here — this PC's Ollama answers any page that asks. Start Ollama first if it isn't running.
exhibits.blurb: Fast and Pro modes, photo messages, and a free local model by default — no API credit needed.

exhibits.title: Project:Filma
exhibits.note: Its FAQ bot works here too — it asks your local gemma4 model through Ollama, so Ollama needs to be running.
exhibits.blurb: The landing page for a video tool that renders footage from a prompt or a script on your own machine.

exhibits.title: TinyCalc
exhibits.short: A calculator in 3 KB of C
exhibits.note: A console program, so it can't run in a browser — this is its landing page.
exhibits.blurb: A whole calculator in a 3 KB Windows program, built from one C file.

exhibits.title: FileMaker Beta
exhibits.note: Built as a desktop app. Here it keeps its work in Aviary instead of a file — saving to a file, CSV export and printing invoices need its desktop shell.
exhibits.blurb: A small office suite in one page: spreadsheets with fonts and alignment, a ledger of income and expenses, and invoices with clients and due dates.

exhibits.title: Battery Charging
exhibits.blurb: A battery icon charging, all in CSS — one of the earliest pages in the Collection.

exhibits.title: Aviary · the landing page
exhibits.blurb: The browser you're in, built out of its own Liquid Glass — and its two phases: Alpha, with Alpha Builds 1 to 5, then Beta.

exhibits.title: Aviary · Phase 0
exhibits.blurb: Both Safari looks against both tab layouts, in light and dark, drawn before any of Aviary was written.

exhibits.title: The CoWork Gazette
exhibits.blurb: A front page for a birthday.

exhibits.title: Grant's Birthday Home Page
exhibits.blurb: Happy birthday, the way a home page said it in 1999.
